scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (eight engineers)

motion.text: The team conducts a non-blocking Lintwise trial on its monorepo, measuring rule coverage, actionable findings, false positives, build time, and queue impact. Any required pre-merge rules require a later decision based on trial results, with explicit ownership, blocking criteria, CI limits, dispute handling, and a rollback path.

objectors.reason: The motion mandates Lintwise before validating coverage and CI impact; on my previous team, it caught real bugs but added about four minutes to CI.
The motion mandates Lintwise before validation, without defined CI time limits or evidence of its impact on build time and queue length.
We have not validated Lintwise’s secret-detection rules against our known test-key incident before making it mandatory.
The motion requires Lintwise before we have validated its rules, false-positive rates, and impact on our 11-minute CI builds.
We have not validated whether Lintwise catches our actual pipeline failure cases, which is essential before making it mandatory.
The motion requires adoption before validating rule coverage, false-positive rates, ownership, and CI impact.
The motion still requires Lintwise immediately, without clarifying which validated rules would block merges or who would own them.

chairQuestions.topic: Findings and CI overhead in prior use
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Priya, what bugs did Lintwise catch, how often, and how comparable was that setup to our monorepo?
Jin, what existing merge-policy provisions cover blocking criteria, check ownership, disputes, and exceptions?

reminders.quote: My notes confirm that Lintwise includes a secret-detection rule set that would have flagged the hard-coded test key that reached main last quarter and had to be rotated.
My notes show that our pipeline code has no static checks today, and two outages last year came from typos in config keys.
